newsitem.title: USA: Intel cuts chip prices up to 48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Intel cuts chip prices up to 48 pct.

text.p: Intel Corp Monday cut prices on some of its oldest microprocessors by as much as 48 percent but the reductions were more modest on Intel's newest models.

The Santa Clara, Calif.-based chip giant said it cut prices on its 200 megahertz Pentium chips by 48 percent to $257 from $498 and trimmed prices on its 166 megahertz Pentium Pro chips by 34.2 percent to $412.
The price cuts, which are announced every quarter by Intel, were much more modest for the company's new line of Pentium chips with MMX multimedia technology.
The 200 megahertz Pentium chip with MMX technology dropped 8.7 percent to $492 while the top of the line 200 megahertz Pentium Pro chip was unchanged at $1,035.

Industry analysts said Intel's price cuts were in line with market expectations and the company's projection two weeks ago when it said the reductions would be similar to the cuts announced in February.
"This is exactly in line with expectations," Montgomery Securities analyst Jonathan Joseph said, adding, on average the cuts represent a 14 percent drop from previous levels.

Intel typically uses price cuts to clear out inventory for some of its older chips. Next month, the company is expected to unveil a new microprocessor called the Pentium II, which essentially combines the power of the Pentium Pro with the multimedia technology of the MMX.
Intel said prices for the Pentium II chips would be announced when the chips are included.
